goal.statement: Govern a delivery scope change and record customer acceptance evidence, without any of it touching the signed commercial record.
goal.outcome: A delivery team that can replan under a governed decision, hand a commercial change to the people who own pricing, and hold defensible evidence of what a customer said about the work.

metric.name: share_of_scope_changes_with_a_recorded_decision
metric.definition: Proportion of delivery scope changes that carry an approved or rejected change request with a stated reason, over changes observed in the period.
metric.target: stated by the delivery organization; this plan does not invent one

observedFacts.statement: The delivery package already owns governed change requests, immutable plan revisions and a commercial-change handoff, offered read-only as delivery-change-management@1.
Acceptance is recorded by a user actor against a frozen scope fingerprint. The schema states it is not an authenticated customer action, not a legal signature and not authorization to bill.
A change with commercial consequence raises an immutable candidate and stops; no Quote, Order, Contract or Subscription is created or altered by the delivery package.
No commercial amendment, invoice, payment or billing-eligibility record type exists anywhere in this application.

derivedMetrics.statement: Share of scope changes carrying a decided change request, computed from the change-request records rather than from any new instrumentation.

assumptions.statement: A delivery lead records a change request at the time the change is agreed, rather than reconstructing it later from memory.
The contact reference recorded on an acceptance request is the person the business treats as speaking for the customer on that scope.

inferences.statement: Because the package can raise a commercial candidate but cannot amend anything, the pending_commercial_followup state is the only place a commercial change can stall — so that is where a reviewer should look, not in the quote history.
Because the request freezes its scope and the evidence binds to that fingerprint, the defensibility of an acceptance record comes from the freeze rather than from who clicked it.

recommendations.statement: Configure and extend the delivery package rather than modelling change management anywhere else: the domain already has an owner, and a second model would split the evidence.
Give the commercial team a standing view of outstanding change candidates, because nothing in delivery will ever resolve one.

unavailableEvidence.statement: The baseline share of governed scope changes cannot be computed for work delivered before change requests existed.
unavailableEvidence.reason: Change requests begin at M14b2; earlier scope changes left no record, and a reconstruction would be an invention rather than evidence.

unavailableEvidence.statement: Whether the person who accepted was authorized by the customer to accept cannot be reported.
unavailableEvidence.reason: There is no authentication, tenancy or RBAC in this framework, and no customer portal. The record states who a user actor asserted accepted, and nothing more.

unavailableEvidence.statement: Whether a raised commercial change was ever quoted, agreed or invoiced cannot be reported.
unavailableEvidence.reason: No commercial amendment or billing runtime exists; the candidate is where this application's knowledge stops.

decisions.rationale: The delivery package already owns governed change, plan revisions and the commercial handoff. Using it is configuration of what exists, not new modelling.
The evidence exists; what a reviewer needs is a view that shows the frozen scope and states the acceptance disclaimers on screen rather than in a document nobody opens.

steps.description: Record every delivery scope change as a change request with a stated reason, and decide it as a human before any replanning happens.
Route a change with commercial consequence to the commercial team through the candidate the approval raises, and review the outstanding candidates as a standing queue.
Show the frozen acceptance scope and the recorded outcome together, with the limits of that record stated beside it rather than assumed.

checks: every scope change in the period carries a decided change request with a stated reason
no commercial record differs before and after a commercial change is handed off
an acceptance record names the frozen scope it answers, and the screen states what that record is not
a rejected acceptance leaves completed execution untouched, and a replan produces a new scope fingerprint

artifacts.description: The change and acceptance section, showing the frozen scope and the disclaimers that bound what it means.
What each record means, and the four things acceptance evidence is not.

limitations.message: Nothing in this plan resolves a commercial change. The candidate is where delivery's knowledge stops, and no amendment runtime exists to consume it yet.
Acceptance records who a user actor asserted accepted. No customer is authenticated, and no legal weight is claimed.
